title: Honor bee's exit-0 repair verdicts in the OpenCode belt
action: S3 judge, blocker F2: bee-guard.ts treats every exit 0 as a plain allow and discards stdout, so bee's DOMINANT enforcement path is inert on OpenCode — model_guard.rs:146-152 repairs a dispatch via hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput at exit 0, write_guard/main.rs:385-410 returns permissionDecision ask (its own comment: ask, never allow) at exit 0, and :413-429 returns a reservation warning as additionalContext. Per decision D6: parse the blocking hook's stdout JSON and (a) apply hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput onto output.args so the repair lands, (b) map permissionDecision ask to a THROW carrying bee's reason — OpenCode's tool.execute.before is two-valued, and ask-as-allow drops the guard, (c) surface additionalContext to the session instead of dropping it (advisory log at minimum; name the chosen surface). Unparseable stdout on a blocking hook is a THROW, never a silent allow. Also fix judge F6: bee-guard.ts:338's `output.message.id` dereference inside the chat.message advisory handler sits outside any try — an advisory surface must never be able to throw. Update the discovery.md hook table rows whose failure policy this changes, and delete the now-stale gap entries the fix closes (the unread on-allow stdout repairs entry). Leave the test file to oc-9.
